1. Whether reporters of local newspapers be allowed to see the judgment?

 

2.      To be referred to the Reporter or not?

 

JUSTICE J.D. KAPOOR, PRESIDENT (ORAL)   On account of having sold a defective refrigerator the District Forum has vide impugned order dated 15-09-2003 directed respondent No. 2 to replace compressor with a similar model purchased by the appellant with fresh warranty and to ensure that the refrigerator is in proper working order and further that the appellant shall return the defective compressor to the respondent and the respondent shall pay Rs. 1,000/- as compensation and cost of litigation.

2. Feeling dissatisfied with the impugned order the appellant has preferred this appeal.

3. Allegations of the appellant before the District Forum, in brief, were that he had purchased a refrigerator under the exchange scheme of Godrej GE Appliances from respondent No.1 on 23-11-1997 for Rs. 12,200/-. The refrigerator was under

warranty for a period of 1 years and a service contract was entered into with the respondent for four years. However, from August 2000 the machine was not functioning satisfactorily and he lodged several complaints with respondent No.1 who in turn directed him to the manufacturer, respondent No.2. Each time the complaint was lodged the technician of the respondent came and changed the gas, or replaced one or the other component of the fridge. Despite all this the fridge did not function satisfactorily. On 12-04-2003 the technician of the respondent replaced the compressor and relay system of the fridge for which the appellant paid a sum of Rs. 3,080/-. However, no guarantee for the new compressor was given to the appellant. He further alleged that the changed compressor was not a new one but a repaired one and also he was not given the old parts that had been changed. The appellant therefore claimed deficiency of service and prayed that the respondent be directed to refund Rs. 15,238/- which is the amount paid by the appellant i.e. 12,200/- + Rs. 3,038/-.

4. As against this the version of the respondent was that complaint is hopelessly barred by time as complainant purchased the refrigerator on 23rd November 1997 and the first complaint regarding the non-functioning of the fridge was received on 8th August 2000, 2 years after the purchase.

On 17th August the compressor and relay system were found to be defective and the same were changed.

It was agreed that the appellant made several complaints to the respondent, but each time the technician visited the premises the refrigerator was found to be in good working condition and since the appellant was complaining regarding the non-cooling, the gas was charged free of cost. As for the changed compressor the appellant had been informed that they would be replacing it with a used compressor, as a new one would cost much more than Rs. 3,000/-. It was denied that the respondents were fooling the appellant or there had been any deficiency of service and that the complaint merits dismissal with costs.

5. Perusal of the impugned order shows that the appellant had for the first time made complaint after three years of the purchase of the refrigerator and subsequently he made several complaints and placed large number of job cards showing that he had been making complaint to the respondent and each time gas was changed. On 12-04-2003 the compressor and the relay system was changed. It is also observed that despite changing compressor of the refrigerator the respondents were not able to completely rectify the defect to the satisfaction of the appellant. The District Forum has given categorical finding that respondent has committed deficiency in service and directed the respondent No. 2 to replace the compressor with a similar model and to ensure that the refrigerator is in proper working order. The failure to rectify the defect or malfunctioning of the refrigerator amounts to deficiency in service.

6. However, the request of the appellant for refund of the cost of the refrigerator was declined on the premise that it was purchased in the year 1997 and was in warranty for one year and in service contract for four years.

7. Be that as it may, the fact remains that the refrigerator sold by the respondent suffered from various defects which could not be rectified in spite of several complaints. It is misconceived notion that goods purchased by the consumer cannot be replaced or the price thereof cannot be refunded unless and until the manufacturing defect is brought beyond the warranty period. The concept of warranty is that dealer is entitled to charge from the consumer for the repairs and if the defects in the goods continue during the warranty period or after the period of warranty for years together goods has to be declared defective goods as conceptualized by section 2(1)(f) of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 which means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or under any contract, express or implied, or as is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to any goods.

8. In such type of cases we have taken a view that cost of the goods should be refunded so as to end the dispute once for all as replacement of any defective goods by new goods is not a solution as such replacement of the goods may not be upto to the satisfaction of the consumer and this may relegate the parties to a second bout of litigation.

9. However, in view of the fact that refrigerator was purchased in the year 1997 and was suffering from several defects even after three years or so the respondent is liable to compensate the appellant adequately. In view of the sufferings and large number of job cards the physical discomfort, mental agony and harassment, emotional sufferings and other sufferings suffered by the appellant, we deem that lump sum compensation of Rs. 10,000/- would meet the ends of justice.

10. Payment shall be made within one month from the date of receipt of this order.

11. Appeal is allowed to the aforesaid extent.

12. A copy of the order as per the statutory requirements be forwarded to the parties free of charge and also to the concerned District Forum and thereafter the file be consigned to Record Room.

13. Announced on the 1st February, 2008.

 

(Justice J.D. Kapoor) President     (Rumnita Mittal) Member jj
